Head of Prep Welcome
I am delighted to welcome you to our world at Sutton High Prep School. Girls here do better because they feel better. We combine exceptional academic results with state-of-the-art facilities, incredible opportunities, and magical, joyful learning.
Courage: The First Step Forward
Every great journey begins with courage. For your daughter, that means stepping into a new environment where she’s seen, heard, and understood. We begin by getting to know her – her interests, her passions, and how she learns best – through personal tours and Open Events. By the time she joins us, she’s not just starting school; she’s entering a space where she already belongs.
Truth: Seeing Is Believing
Truth reveals itself in experience. When your daughter arrives on her first day, she begins to explore our exceptional facilities: an indoor swimming pool, full-size sports hall, dance studio, science labs, and a purpose-built outdoor learning area surrounded by green spaces. It’s a place designed to spark discovery and wonder, where she can breathe the wild air.
Joy: Where the Magic Happens
Joy is at the heart of learning. This is where the magic begins – girls embrace a growth mindset and discover their Prep School Superpowers. The girls learn to face challenges with resilience and optimism, they are empowered to take a risk and be flexible of mind, and they are kind and empathetic to their community. Our girls do better because they feel better.
Joy in Action: Learning That Comes Alive
Joy continues beyond the classroom. With over 50 extra-curricular clubs, exciting trips, drama productions, competitive sports fixtures, and inspiring guest speakers, every day is filled with opportunity. We bring learning to life – vibrantly, meaningfully, and memorably.
I warmly invite you to visit us and experience the spirit of our school firsthand. It would be a pleasure to show you around, introduce you to our community, and share the courage, truth and joy that shapes every girl’s journey here.
Emily Ruiz Head of Prep School

About us
Welcome to Sutton High School. We are an independent day school for girls from 3-18, part of the GDST family since we were founded in 1884. Girls here love their school, learn with joy and want each other to succeed.
Head’s Welcome
I am delighted to welcome you to Sutton High School. We combine joyful learning, outstanding academic results and excellence in pastoral care.
Our Manifesto and Strategy
We have been educating and inspiring girls for over 139 years. In that time, we have developed a strong sense of who we are and what we stand for.
Our Pioneering History
We are part of a pioneering movement that started over150 years ago. Together with our sister GDST schools, we defied Victorian attitudes to women by providing a rigorous academic curriculum for local girls.
GDST
We are proud to be part of the Girls’ Day School Trust, a family of 25 schools across England and Wales.
Examination Results
Our entirely bespoke curriculum enables every individual girl to maximise her potential in public examinations. We are proud of our students and our teachers for achieving outstanding results year after year.
Why All Girls?
The Girls Day School Trust, of which we are part, has recently released a research paper which outlines the argument for girls’ schools and girls-only education. You can read the full paper at the bottom of the page.
GDST Space Tech
Hosted by Sutton High School and managed across multiple participating GDST Computer Science departments.
Term Dates
Term dates, INSET days and Bank Holidays
Staff
We have a team of specialist, expert staff who ensure that all our students maximise their potential, both inside the classroom and beyond. They know and celebrate our girls as individuals, love their work and teach with joy.
Governors
Our board of governors provides support, guidance and critical oversight to the Headmistress and the school. The governors bring valuable expertise from various professional fields and we are very grateful for their commitment and their capabilities.
Venue Hire
Sutton High School has a wide variety of facilities available for hire. Our sports complex offers a 500m2 sports hall, 25m x 8m swimming pool and a dance studio with mirrored wall, sound system and sprung flooring. We also offer 6 external tennis courts, 5 netball courts and a Multi Use Games Astroturf.
School Transport
From our own, newly enhanced, school minibus service for girls in year 3 and above, to the wide range of public transport options available, there are plenty of opportunities for a sustainable journey to school.
Vacancies
We have an amazing team at Sutton High School. Just like our students, staff are known and celebrated for who they are, and for what they can bring to the school. As a group, we are friendly, supportive and dedicated to providing an outstanding education for our girls, both inside the classroom and beyond.
ISI Inspection Report
The Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) carries out inspections of independent schools on behalf of the Department of Education. We were last inspected in November 2021. You can read Mrs Dawson’s summary and download the inspection report.
Key Dates and Lunch Menu
Find out what’s happening this week across the school and discover what mouth watering treats are on the menu!
School Development Masterplan
An ambitious Masterplan has been formulated comprising of a number of phases, to create facilities, resources and learning spaces that will wholly support the forward thinking ethos of the school.
Support for Parents
A resource hub for supporting your child through difficult stages.

Head’s welcome
Inspiring individuals
We inspire and nurture individuality – you will not find a particular ‘type’ here. Our girls learn to find their own voice and be confident in who they are. Our size allows us to know and value every girl and we place enormous emphasis on both self-respect and respect for others. We know that girls do better when they feel better, so their wellbeing is our central focus. Every girl will find her own path here and she will forge that path with support from passionate and dedicated staff, committed to her success.
A broad and bespoke curriculum
Our girls work hard and they enjoy learning, which leads to excellent academic results. From Nursery through to the Sixth Form, lessons are engaging and taught by well-qualified specialist teachers. Students have access to a wide range of subjects across the arts, humanities and STEM, as well as distinctive enrichment opportunities. Learning is personalised for every girl and our small classes allow us to set individual targets to ensure that all girls achieve their best.
A wealth of opportunity
Beyond the classroom, our girls’ experiences are vast and varied. From our many co-curricular clubs to a comprehensive schedule of day-trips and residential visits as far-reaching as the Galapagos Islands, the opportunities are endless. As part of the Girls’ Day School Trust, our girls have access to a much wider network, which offers them trust-wide conferences, competitions and learning opportunities.
I want our school to be a place that ignites a spark in every girl, so that she finds new interests and develops her individual talents.
A sense of belonging
We put girls first and they are able to learn in a productive environment, without gender stereotypes of perceived limitations. Every girl will find her place here as part of a friendly and welcoming school community and our volunteering, charity work and school partnerships ensure that girls are also active participants in our local community. The unique Brains Matter (Prep) and Personal and Social Responsibility (Senior) courses, as well as our award-winning careers provision mean that our girls are fully prepared for the ever-changing world around them and are self-assured, kind and collaborative.
Sutton High School is a school where girls are both interesting and interested. Visitors often comment on the warmth and vibrancy of the school and the best way to experience this is to come and visit! I very much look forward to welcoming you.
Beth Dawson Head
Year 8 parent
Come and see for yourself
We hold Open Events throughout the year so you can meet our girls, hear from the Head and ask any questions you want. It’s the best way to find out what makes us different.

ISI Inspection Report
The Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) carries out inspections of independent schools on behalf of the Department of Education. You can read Mrs Dawson’s summary of our recent inspection, which took place in November 2024 and download the inspection report below.
In 2023, the ISI re-worked their inspection framework and we were inspected under this ‘Framework 2023’. Schools are no longer graded (e.g. good/excellent) but are now inspected against whether each of the Independent Schools Standards are met or not met. However, in special circumstances, the inspection team may choose to recognise a school with a judgement of ‘Significant Strength’. Such judgments are rare and I am very pleased that Sutton High School has been recognised as having a “Significant Strength”, which is identified as the following:
Leaders monitor and analyse assessment data thoroughly and with precision to inform teachers so that they respond to the specific needs of pupils and groups very swiftly and highly effectively. Leaders quickly adapt and revise both the curriculum and timetable in response to their analysis of data, so that pupils’ needs and aspirations are consistently met extremely well. The school’s highly effective use of and response to data is a significant strength of the school.
All Independent Schools Standards were met and our recommended next step (we were only given one of these) is to ensure that all inspection reports are always readily available via our website (we had only placed the last two reports on the website, rather than the last ten years of reports).
From the quality of the academic education we offer to the pastoral support, careers advice and co-curricular activities available, we are extremely proud to help produce confident, articulate, happy young women.
This success is testament to the dedication and commitment of our wonderful staff who work incredibly hard to provide a first-class experience for every student, something that is only made possible by the support shown by our parent body.
If you are a current student or parent then I thank you on behalf of all the staff for your part in making our school such a happy, vibrant and successful environment. If you are a prospective student or parent, I very much look forward to welcoming you to Sutton High School where our core values of courage, truth and joy are always in evidence.

Explorers Leader

What do the governors do?
The main responsibilities of the governors are:
To be critical friends of the school
To support the Headmistress and her staff
How is the school governed?
Sutton High School, along with the other schools of the Girls’ Day School Trust, is administered by the Council of the Trust. Each school has its own School Governing Board (SGB) whose Chair is appointed by the Council. New governors are appointed by the existing SGB. Each governor serves up to three terms of three years each.
How can I get in touch?
The Chair of our board of governors is Ms Catherine Clarke. Should you wish to contact Ms Clarke direct, please write to her at: Sutton High School, 55 Cheam Road, Sutton SM1 2AX
Our governors
Ms Catherine Clarke (Chair)
Catherine Clarke attended school and university in Ireland, undertaking both her undergraduate and post-graduate studies at Trinity College Dublin, where she obtained degrees in civil and structural engineering. After having worked as an engineer in the UK for a number of years at a multinational engineering consultancy firm, and having obtained “chartered engineer” status, Catherine took the decision to return to university to study law, qualifying as a solicitor in 1996. Catherine has spent her entire legal career in the City, specialising in the law relating to major infrastructure projects. She currently works in-house at a large City firm, a role which she combines with sitting as a part-time district judge on the London and South East Circuit. As a parent to an SHS alumna, Catherine brings the “parent perspective” to her role as an SHS governor, alongside her experience in legal analysis and regulatory compliance matters.
Mr William Rogers
William Rogers is a trained ISI Inspector and was Deputy Head of Emmanuel School. Prior to that he held a variety of senior roles at Wallington County Grammar, where he taught for over twenty years. His interests include reading, photography, cycling and keeping fit. He also enjoys walking and going to the theatre, and is a qualified ski instructor.
Mrs Charlotte Sallabank
Charlotte Sallabank was brought up in Edinburgh and graduated from King’s College, London with a degree in Mathematics and Chemistry. After working for three years in corporate finance for an international bank, Charlotte retrained as a solicitor, specialising in corporate tax. Charlotte is a chartered tax advisor and is a partner in the London office of a US law firm. In addition to advising on tax, Charlotte is the pro bono chair of the London office and is a member of the steering committee of the firm’s Women’s Leadership Forum which supports the advancement of women lawyers at the firm through mentoring and career development programmes.
Charlotte’s four daughters have all attended Sutton High – the youngest left in July 2022, marking the end of a 23 year continuous period as a Sutton High parent and 26 years as a GDST parent. Nida worked as an economic consultant at EY for a decade, later working with charities and philanthropic funds in London and Miami. Nida recently trained as a teacher of English as an Additional Language, and teaches English to refugees and migrants.
Nida is married with two children. Her daughter attended nursery and junior school at Sutton High. Being a Governor at Sutton High is a way of giving back to the school that has made such a positive impact on Nida and her daughter.
Mrs Georgie Franklin
Georgie Franklin (née Altman) attended two GDST schools, Putney High School and Notting Hill and Ealing High school. From there she went on to read Modern History at the University of Oxford.
After graduating she began a career in the commercial world, initially in the retail sector both in legacy businesses and in the high growth ecommerce sector. From there she moved into advertising and marketing strategy, advising some of the UK’s biggest businesses (including easyJet and O2).
For the past 7 years she’s worked at Google in its commercial arm in London. In this capacity she leads the relationship with some of the UK’s biggest retailers and has responsibility for growing and developing their business with Google.
Georgie is thrilled that as a governor she is able to give back to the GDST, which gave her so much.
Ms Karis Parker
Karis was brought up in Islington, London and attended St Mary’s University for her BA in Primary Education. Karis has a passion for Special Educational Needs and inclusive schools. In her role as SENDCo, Karis has been one of the designated safeguarding leads for her school and supports SHS as a safeguarding champion.

Sarah has lived in the South West London area all her life and attended Putney High School.
From there she studied Medicine at the Westminster Hospital Medical School qualifying in 1982.
Having always wanted to be a General Practitioner, Sarah completed general practice training in Fulham and joined the Church Lane Practice in Merton Park as a Partner in 1986. In 2015 the Church Lane Practice merged and became part of the Nelson Medical Practice in South Wimbledon. This is the largest General Practice in Merton serving just over 32,000 patients including current and past Sutton High School students. Sarah is currently the joint chair of the practice Governing Body.
After 40 years experience as an NHS G.P, and as a past GDST pupil, Sarah looks forward to contributing positively to Sutton High School as a Governor and on health issues in particular.

Kathy has 3 adult children and 4 grandchildren, and alongside some insight into leadership and innovation, her main focus will be on the well-being of all involved in the school community.

Erin will pursue her passion for Outdoor Leadership at the University of Cumbria, learning in the mountains of the UNESCO World Heritage Site, the Lake District National Park.With the Creative Industries growing at nearly four times the rate of our national economy, it is no surprise that several pupils will be pursuing this direction, having gained places at Russell Group universities. Pastoral enrichment
At Sutton High we cherish individuality. You will be celebrated and supported for who you are every step of the way. We have a strong culture of girls supporting girls in every aspect of school life and beyond; our girls want each other to succeed. Our Sixth Form goes far beyond outstanding A-level teaching so that every girl leaves us as a confident woman, ready to face her future with total faith in who she is as an individual.

Tutor groups are small, friendly and close-knit. They are made up of both Year 12 and Year 13 students, so you can share experiences at key times and form strong bonds across year groups.
You will have regular one-to-one tutorials with your form tutor and they will be available for you every day to offer both academic and pastoral support. Your form tutor will come to understand you exceptionally well, and this insight means that Sutton High UCAS references are completely unique and personal.
Form tutors are handpicked to work at Sixth Form level, and they are experts in identifying and solving the issues faced by girls at this stage of their lives.
Your wellbeing is at the heart of what we do. We enrol all girls in the ground-breaking GDST Positive Project to help to promote good mental health. We also have an in-house school counsellor and medical manager on hand whenever you need them.
We’re a friendly bunch!

GCSE Results 2026
An outstanding 23% of all grades were awarded at Grade 9 (4 times the national average), while more than two-thirds of all results were at Grades 9-7 (equivalent to A/A*). Almost half of all grades achieved were at Grades 9-8, the equivalent of the former A.
There was also plenty of individual success to celebrate, with ten students achieving straight Grade 9s and a further twenty students securing a clean sweep of Grades 9-7.
The results reflect Sutton High School’s commitment to offering a broad and ambitious curriculum, with particularly strong performances across STEM subjects. In Computer Science, 75% of grades were awarded at Grade 9, while across Biology, Chemistry and Physics, 50% of grades achieved were Grade 9s. Mathematics students also excelled, with 55% of grades awarded at Grade 9.

Value Added
Our most important examination statistic is for ‘Value Added’. This is the measure of improvement that our pupils make from joining the school in Year 7 to achieving their A Level results. We admit girls with a wide range of ability to Sutton High School, and we challenge them to achieve their own personal best.
On their first day of Year 7, all pupils (across the country) take a baseline test which uses statistical analysis to predict, based on their ability scores, the results they have the potential to obtain for GCSE. A school’s ‘Value Added’ score is the difference between these initial predictions of potential and the actual results obtained by pupils for GCSE or A Level.
At Sutton High this score is high, meaning that, on average, girls here attain higher grades, in every subject, than their ability score on entry to our school and pupils with lower starting points make particularly strong progress. As an example, in History, our ‘Value Added’ score is 1.1, meaning that a pupil arriving at Sutton High School with a prediction of a 6 in History, is likely to attain a 7 or above at GCSE. This is referred to as the value we add, through teaching and through the education we offer. We believe this reflects the dedicated work of our pupils and the excellent, personalised support they are given by our staff.

Our Pioneering History
From the early days, our girls went to Oxford, Cambridge and London universities, having been provided with opportunities that were previously unheard of for girls, like studying chemistry in laboratories. Groundbreaking female scientists, writers and thinkers have passed through our doors, challenging perceptions and shattering stereotypes.
Our history is who we are and, as part of the GDST, we remain leaders in girls’ education to this day.
Take a peek here at some of the highlights from our recent 140th anniversary celebrations.
You can watch Mrs Sue James, our archivist, talk about the unexpected treasure that is our school archive as she recalls anecdotal stories of the people who make up the fascinating history of our school. She has also written a short history of the school below. If you would like to get in touch with her, please contact s.james@sut.gdst.net
The Equal Rights of Women
In 1871 Maria Grey, one of the pioneers of female education, made an appeal for “the equal right of all women to the education recognised as the best for human beings”. Her bid for equality led to the founding of the Girls’ Public Day School Company (now the GDST) a year later.
Sutton High School was the twenty eighth such school, opening on Thursday 17 January 1884. Sutton itself had changed in the previous 50 years from a village to a town due to the building of the railway line, but it was also considered a health resort due to its springs and its proximity to the Downs.
There was enough interest amongst the growing population for the GPDSC to open a school and the company responded by buying a Victorian villa, Park House, in Cheam Road, which is the white building at the centre of the site.
The First Headmistress
Margaret Chalmers Whyte was the first Headmistress; she too shared the vision of Maria Grey. She had reacted against the restrictions of being a female brought up in the mid nineteenth century when women, including herself, were not admitted to university. It was her wish and that of the GPDSC to challenge this male dominance and to produce what Miss Whyte called “a woman of all round culture and many-sided sympathies”.
There were 80 girls in the first cohort; one pupil recorded that the opening day was a little chaotic as Miss Whyte did not know exactly who would come. We are told in the first magazine that the girls “wandered up and down the passages gazing with mingled awe and curiosity on the large classrooms with their formal desks and many other modern appliances.” It soon became very clear that the villa was too small and within two years the Study (then the school hall) and the tower classrooms had been added. These were opened by the patron of the GPDSC, Queen Victoria’s daughter, Princess Louise. If you look very carefully above the old front door you can see the date when it was built.
Innovators in Science Education
Within six months the school distinguished itself by entering girls for public examinations in a variety of subjects. Suitably qualified staff in traditional male subjects were difficult to find but the school was fortunate to employ an inspirational science teacher in 1895, Miss Annette Hunt, who stayed for over 30 years. Before retiring in 1928 she helped design a suite of laboratories which were considered to be some of the best in English girls’ schools.
“This Door Opens Outwards”
Miss Whyte was not only interested in the academic life of the school but in sport, acting and giving musical concerts. Amongst the gardens, the first tennis courts were laid out by girls using paint brushes. Charitable work was started immediately, with boxes of toys and clothing being sent to the London hospitals for children and, in the summer term, the girls brought in flowers which were then distributed to local charities. The sign above the old front door, This Door Opens Outwards, became a metaphor for the school’s links to the local community.
With Courage, With Truth, With Joy
Since the opening day in 1884, Sutton High School has educated thousands of girls and has continued through two world wars. The girls of 1884 would not recognise the purple uniform, the facilities, the iPads. We would not recognise some of the games they played, their formal language and the method of teaching.
Yet the school motto, ‘Fortiter, Fideliter, Feliciter’, first adopted for the school’s twenty-first birthday in 1905, remains a constant in school life today. Both the girls and staff of 2019 know the meaning of the three Latin words off by heart: with courage, with truth, with joy.

Senior Leadership Staff
We have a team of specialist, expert staff who ensure that all our students maximise their potential, both inside the classroom and beyond. They know and celebrate our girls as individuals, love their work and teach with joy.
Senior Team
Beth Dawson – Head
Beth has been a teacher for twenty-five years, having taught at Surbiton High School, Reigate Grammar School and Commonweal School prior to joining Emanuel School in Battersea, where she held a number of roles including Director of Scholars and Head of Creative Arts. Beth joined Sutton High School in 2017 as Deputy Head and has been Head since 2019. She trained in Drama and Education, knowing from an early age that teaching was a career she wanted to pursue. As a specialist in Drama, Music and English, Beth is a passionate advocate for the arts and has directed several Edinburgh Fringe productions, with a particular focus on modern retellings of Greek tragedies. She is a TEDX speaker, having researched the importance of self-expression and identity for teenage girls. Outside school, Beth loves to sing and can be found belting out karaoke classics! At Sutton High, Beth has developed a focus on the core values of Courage, Truth and Joy and on every pupil being not only known, but understood. Belonging at school is vital, and Beth believes that it is this sense of belonging and community that makes Sutton High amazing.
Emily Ruiz – Head of Prep
Emily became Head of Sutton High Prep School in September 2025, returning to a community she knows well and values deeply. She previously taught at Sutton for many years before moving to Croydon High School as Deputy Head of Juniors, where she gained extensive leadership experience. An alumna of Sutton High, Emily is proud to uphold the values of the GDST and is strongly aligned with its commitment to developing confident, curious and fiercely independent girls. She is delighted to be back at Sutton High Prep, a school she describes as kind, vibrant and nurturing, offering girls an exceptional foundation for their educational journey. Beyond the classroom, Emily enjoys country walks with her family and her cockapoo, Peggy, who also serves as the school’s pastoral dog. She is a keen netball player and values teamwork, a principle she strives to foster throughout the Prep School. Emily is extremely proud to lead Sutton High Prep and to work in partnership with the girls and their families. She is always happy to talk and can be found on the school gate each day, warmly welcoming pupils and parents alike.
Daniel Vickery – Director of Operations
Daniel Vickery has been part of Sutton High School since 2016. He brings almost 20 years of estates, facilities, ICT and operational leadership across both education and government sectors to the Senior Leadership Team. A graduate of London Metropolitan University with a BA (Hons) in Business, supported by professional qualifications in fire safety and health and safety management, he now serves as Director of Operations for both Sutton High School GDST and Brighton Girls GDST. During his time at Sutton High School, Daniel has overseen major capital developments, strengthened compliance and safety frameworks, and enhanced the efficiency and effectiveness of the school’s operational services, while also leading the school’s commercial development activities. Drawing on his well established project management skills, he delivers complex initiatives smoothly and strategically. He is recognised for his commitment to creating a safe, well run and future focused environment in which students and staff can thrive.
Michelle Kirk – Director of Finance
Michelle joined Sutton High School in October 2025 as Director of Finance. A qualified Chartered Accountant (ACA), she brings extensive financial expertise gained across both commercial and charitable organisations. MIchelle began her career with KPMG before moving into senior finance leadership roles in the commercial sector. She later transitioned into the charity sector, where she held key financial positions at the National Theatre and Martlets Hospice in Brighton. Having joined the Girls’ Day School Trust (GDST) in 2021, Michelle was appointed Director of Finance for Brighton Girls and Sutton High School in 2025. She leads the finance and catering functions, providing strategic financial leadership that supports informed decision-making, operational excellence, and long-term sustainability. Michelle ensures that Sutton High is well positioned to invest in outstanding educational opportunities, enabling students to achieve their full potential both inside and beyond the classroom. Away from school, Michelle enjoys gardening and reading, although much of her spare time is happily spent supporting her children at their sporting fixtures.
Laura James – Director of Marketing and Communications
Laura joined Sutton High School in 2020, bringing with her a wealth of experience in large-scale corporate events, marketing and publishing. Her background has provided the perfect preparation for the fast-paced and varied world of school life, where no two days are ever quite the same. Having grown up in a family of educators, working in education has always felt like a natural calling. Passionate about making a difference to girls’ lives, Laura firmly believes that Sutton High is a place where girls are empowered to thrive, grow and achieve their potential. As a strong advocate for girls and women of the future, she is proud to play a role in sharing the stories, successes and opportunities that make the school such a special community. Outside of school, Laura is a keen runner and can often be found out on the trails or training for her next challenge. With two very active children, she also loves spending time with her family in the great outdoors.
Elizabeth Clark – Deputy Head Pastoral
Elizabeth has played a pivotal role in developing and shaping the pastoral care and wellbeing provision at Sutton High School. She is passionate that each pupil navigates her teenage years in a school which is supportive of individual needs and provides the highest quality guidance when decisions have to be taken. The teams delivering pastoral care and wellbeing are amongst the best in their field; led by Elizabeth, they work as a close, collaborative team to ensure that each pupil is known and supported for who she is. Elizabeth taught in both the state and independent sector before joining Sutton High as Head of Sixth Form in September 2000. She has taught Economics and Business Studies throughout her career and currently teaches Economics at A level. The highlight of her week though is teaching Geography in Year 7.
Susan Lawlor-Price – Deputy Head Academic
Susan joined Sutton High School in 2017 as Director of Studies and became Deputy Head (Academic) two years later. With more than 20 years of teaching experience, she still loves the energy of school life and the fact that no two days are ever the same. Susan has dedicated her career to girls’ education and her commitment to this pathway stems from her own experience as one of the few female students in A level STEM classes and later while studying Chemistry at the University of Oxford. A strong advocate of growth mindset, Susan also encourages every student to embrace challenge, develop resilience and believe in their ability to succeed. Outside school, she enjoys escaping into a good book, finding headspace on a 10K run, and the thrill of a rollercoaster ride!
Beth Ashton – Deputy Head of Prep
Beth has worked in education for over ten years and joined Sutton High School in 2023 as Deputy Head of Prep. She leads the academic vision of the Prep School, oversees teaching and learning, supports curriculum development, and leads Undivided, the GDST Equality, Diversity and Inclusion initiative. She is also responsible for the Prep library and is passionate about fostering a lifelong love of reading through an inclusive and diverse collection of books.
Beth holds an MA in English Literature from the University of Edinburgh and an MA in Children’s Literature from Goldsmiths, University of London. She has collaborated with children’s author Michael Rosen on published research exploring children’s literature and learning. Currently, Beth is undertaking a research fellowship with the International Coalition of Girls’ Schools, supported by the GDST, investigating how creative thinking can help girls thrive across the curriculum, particularly in STEM subjects.
Passionate about combining academic excellence with pastoral care, Beth is committed to helping every child discover their strengths. She leads the Prep School’s Be You vision, promoting creativity, empathy, reflection and resilience, self-efficacy, and critical thinking throughout school life.
Senior School Leadership Team
The Senior School Leadership Team comprises the Head and Deputy Heads of Seniors, in addition to the following staff:
Jenni Dixon – Director of Wellbeing (Year 9-11)
Jenni joined Sutton High School in 2014 as an English Teacher. Drawing on more than 15 years of teaching experience, she understands that students can only truly thrive and make the most of both academic and extracurricular opportunities when they feel well supported pastorally. This belief led her to take on the role of Head of Years 10 and 11 in 2015. Now, as Director of Wellbeing for Years 9 to 11, she leads a Team of experienced Heads of Year and works closely with other Pastoral staff to ensure that every girl feels seen, valued and supported. She is passionate about helping students understand that, when things are not going well, there is a strong network of people around them ready to help. Outside of school, Jenni can usually be found walking Teddy, a black Labrador, who will greet you with great enthusiasm should you ever bump into him.
Lucy Durrant – Director of Digital and Innovation
Lucy joined Sutton High School in 2020 as Academic Deputy Head of the Prep School, before moving to the Senior School in 2023 to take up the role of Director of Digital and Innovation. She is passionate about harnessing technology to enhance teaching and learning, remove barriers and create opportunities for every pupil to thrive. In her current role, she leads the school’s digital strategy and the development of innovative approaches to teaching and learning. Her work focuses on using technology purposefully to improve accessibility, reduce cognitive load and support pupils to become confident, independent learners. She is particularly interested in the opportunities presented by artificial intelligence and is committed to ensuring that AI is used creatively, responsibly and ethically to enhance learning while developing pupils’ critical thinking and digital literacy. Prior to moving into the Senior School, Lucy spent three years as Academic Deputy Head of Sutton High Prep School, leading on curriculum development, teaching and learning and academic strategy. She has over 12 years’ experience in senior leadership across both Prep and Senior School settings, giving her a broad perspective on how pupils’ learning, independence and digital skills develop throughout their education. At the heart of her approach is a belief that technology should make learning more accessible rather than more complicated. She is committed to inspiring pupils to be curious about emerging technologies, understand both their possibilities and responsibilities, and develop the skills, confidence and adaptability they will need to become future-ready learners. Outside of school, Mrs Durrant enjoys spending time with her family and is happiest outdoors, particularly with her horse and dogs.
Ben Essenhigh – Director of Enrichment and Partnerships
Ben leads Enrichment and Partnerships at Sutton High School, shaping the opportunities that help girls discover who they are beyond the classroom. His role encompasses co-curricular provision, educational visits, partnerships and community engagement, Houses and charities, with a particular focus on ensuring that every pupil can access an ambitious and varied range of experiences. A graduate of Leeds College of Music, Ben has worked in education for more than 17 years across the state and independent sectors, holding pastoral, academic and co-curricular leadership roles. He is a Chartered Fellow of the Chartered Management Institute and a Fellow of the Chartered College of Teaching. At Sutton High, he is passionate about creating purposeful and inclusive opportunities that encourage girls to develop confidence, curiosity and independence. Through enrichment, leadership and service, he aims to help every Sutton High girl build a strong sense of self, belonging and readiness to make her mark on the wider world.
Sarah Manser – Director of Wellbeing (Year 7 and 8)
Sarah has worked at Sutton High School for eight years, serving for the past five as Director of Wellbeing for Years 7 and 8. Prior to joining Sutton High School and the GDST, she held roles in both a large state comprehensive and an independent school, where she served as Curriculum and Examination Lead for PE and moderated for one of the country’s largest exam boards.

We are a highly academic school and we inspire girls with our challenging, exciting curriculum from Nursery to Year 6. Girls at Sutton High know what they will be doing when they come into school every single day: learning with joy.
Nursery and Reception (ages 3 – 5)
We believe that early years education should not be ‘just play’. It is vitally important to set girls up for their school journey ahead, and to give them a love of learning for life.
All our Nursery and Reception classes are taught by qualified early years teachers and teaching assistants. We provide a stimulating learning environment and challenge girls to be curious, inquisitive and independent.

Years 1 and 2 (ages 5-7)
As they move into Year 1, we focus on giving girls the strongest possible foundations in English and Mathematics. Other subjects are taught through our bespoke connected curriculum to ensure the girls make links between subjects, develop knowledge and increase the depth of their understanding.
Alongside the class teacher and teaching assistants, girls will continue to experience lessons with subject specialists in French, Music and PE, as well as having weekly swimming lessons in our indoor pool.
Years 3 – 6 (ages 7-11)
From Year 3 onwards, girls begin to prepare for the 11+ transition by having an increasing number of lessons taught by specialist teachers, in specialist classrooms.
Before the end of Year 6, girls secure places and scholarships at our Senior School, other leading independent schools and local grammar schools. Girls complete weekly verbal and non-verbal reasoning lessons from Year 3, but it is our all-round curriculum that ensures we achieve outstanding 11+ results year after year.
We are proud that girls from Sutton High Prep School go on to the next stage of their education with smiles on their faces, a passion for learning and all the tools they need to succeed.

Nursery & Prep
We welcome admissions enquiries throughout the year for entry into any year group and can arrange a personal tour at any time, so there is no need to wait for an Open Morning to come and see us in action.
As a family school, we are proud that girls who join Prep School in Year 3, 4, 5 and 6 will be considered for automatic transfer to Senior School without the requirement to sit our 11+ examination.
Our Prep School Admissions Officer, Mrs Gabrielle Stubbs, is here to help you every step of the way. Please do get in touch: prepadmissions@sut.gdst.net / 020 8225 3021, or make an enquiry here.
Step 1
Come and get to know us. You can either book online for an Open Event or it’s easy to arrange a personal tour with a member of the Prep School leadership team. If you want, you can do both! We look forward to meeting you.
Step 2
To apply for a place, please complete our online application form. You will need to pay a non-refundable registration fee of £150 (or £240 for overseas applications).
Step 3
Entry to Nursery, Reception, Year 1 and Year 2
We do not have entrance assessments for our younger girls as we believe that their ability cannot be meaningfully tested at such a young age.
Instead, you and your daughter will be invited to spend some time with us to confirm that we are the right fit for you. We encourage you to bring your daughter’s last school report, if she has one, to share with us.
We welcome nursery applications all year round. Your daughter can start at the beginning of the autumn, spring, or summer term — whenever works best for your family. We also offer half-term starts to make things even easier. She can join us in the term or half-term after she turns 3. At that point, she’ll be eligible for the Early Years Grant, which covers up to 15 hours of funded care each week.
We’re here to make her first steps into school life happy, gentle, and full of care.
Entry to Years 3, 4, 5 and 6
Girls will be invited to an assessment morning. They will take online tests in verbal and non-verbal reasoning and have an informal meeting with a member of the Prep School leadership team. No preparation is needed for either the tests or the meeting.
Our assessment mornings for Autumn 2026 have now concluded.
Please contact prepadmissions@sut.gdst.net to discuss assessment for Autumn 2026 entry.
Assessment dates for 2027/2028 entry will be released in the autumn.
Our assessment is designed to be a fun, exciting experience. You only need to bring a book your daughter has enjoyed reading, her last school report and something she is proud to talk about.
Step 4
For entry up to Year 2, we will be in touch to confirm our offer shortly after your daughter’s visit to school. Places are offered on a first-come, first-served basis. Girls gain automatic entry into Year 3.
Girls applying for entry to Years 3 and above will be offered a place subject to the results of our entrance assessment. The offer will also indicate if your daughter has been guaranteed a place in our Senior School.
We look forward to welcoming you to Sutton High School!
Entrance registration fee and deposit
From January 2025, a non-refundable registration fee of £150 (£240 for overseas candidates) is charged for taking the entrance examination/assessment and is not transferable from one entrance year or sibling. A deposit of £1,000 (for overseas pupils this is £3000 for Prep School and £5000 for Senior School) is charged on the acceptance of a place and will be retained until the pupil leaves the school. The deposit will not be refunded if the place is not taken up.
